messages:
anna (privacy): Heads-up: DSAR for user u-9c3 — user asked for full deletion. Engineering confirmed primary DB rows removed yesterday but there are references in older nightly snapshots/backups encrypted with CMEK `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/embeddings/cryptoKeys/embeddings-key` v1. Unsure if delete propagation covers cold snapshots; need infra + sec to advise.

sasha (sec-eng): ack. do we have formal proof of deletion (tombstone + purge logs)? right-to-be-forgotten requires reasonable steps. @mike (infra) can you confirm backup lifecycle + KMS rotation history and whether old key versions still allow decryption?

mike (infra): looking now. backups are nightly, retention 90d. snapshots are GCS objects encrypted with the CMEK. rotating key doesn't destroy old versions; old key versions still decrypt unless we destroy them. we also keep a metadata index for fast lookup but it's eventually consistent.

jim (ops): destroying keys is nuclear — breaks all restores. legal will need to sign off. also note: `serviceAccount:backup-restore@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` still has roles/kms.decrypt on that key.

kate (legal): for DSARs we need documented, reasonable steps. Destroying CMEK could be disproportionate if we have lawful retention needs. Can infra support targeted removal of only the specific user's blobs from object storage? If yes, that's preferable.

sasha (sec-eng): proposed workflow: 1) run a targeted scan across backup objects for user id markers (u-9c3) 2) isolate any matching blobs to a quarantine bucket 3) perform secure purge of those blobs and record manifest 4) if anything cannot be purged without key destruction, open retention-exception. Need RBAC: who can run scans? prefer a narrow `privacy-scan` SA.

anna (privacy): +1. User expects response within 30d — tagging as high priority. I'll attach the DSAR ticket and proof of request to the case.

mike (infra): quick adhoc command I'm running to find appearances (inefficient but works):

```
gsutil ls -r gs://redwood-backups/embeddings/** | xargs -n1 -I{} gsutil cat {} | grep -E 'u-9c3'
```

this will be slow for full bucket; alternative is to query the object metadata index (if we can rely on it).

oncall-bot: privacy-scan deploy 0.21.3 scheduled at 18:30 UTC :alarm_clock:

sasha (sec-eng): RBAC change plan: create `roles/backupScanner` with `roles/kms.viewer` and `storage.objects.get` restricted to prefix `backups/embeddings/`. Will open PR and add reviewers from infra + privacy. Also propose adding audit logging for any run.

jim (ops): quick vuln note: found `legacy-restore-sa@redwood` still has broad access to backups. adding to vul triage and will rotate keys/limit scope. no active exploit observed but this is stale-privilege.

kate (legal): we can approve targeted deletion if we receive the scan report plus legal attestation that steps were reasonable. If encryption prevents targeted removal, retention-exception needs to be opened and documented.

anna (privacy): timeline: run scan by EOD, assemble report, and draft deletion manifest. if blobs are found that can't be purged easily we'll open a retention-exception with justification and mitigations. tagging @sasha (sec-eng) @mike (infra) @jim (ops).

sasha (sec-eng): noted. will post PR link + IAM policy diff when ready.

mike (infra): scan finished: found 3 blobs referencing u-9c3 across two snapshots (2026-02-08 and 2026-01-20). creating deletion tasks and a manifest. PR: http://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/452 — moving to deletion queue.
